expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | (SubscriptionBase & { status: 'trialing'; trialEndsAt: Date }) | ... for each status

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each type in the union has only its specific fields paired with SubscriptionBase

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Shows assertNever function with default: return assertNever(sub);

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: function transition(current: Subscription, event: SubscriptionEvent): Subscription { throw new Error('not implemented'); }

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Lists: {status: 'active', cancelReason: '...'}, forgotten switch cases, independent voluntary/reason fields

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Begins with 'What could go wrong with a flatter design' then recommends discriminated union.
